explanations.explanation: The Jordan it is, friend! The LORD says, “…cross over the Jordan into the land that I am giving to the children of Israel.” Moses, Israel's leader, has died, so Joshua is the one who has to get up first. I'd need a minute to stretch before that kind of morning.

The Red Sea is a fair guess, because the Israelites went through it on dry ground in Moses' day (Exodus 14:22). Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. That crossing is behind them, though. This time the LORD names a different water: “…cross over the Jordan…”

The Jabbok is a real river in the Bible. Jacob, who was later called Israel (Genesis 32:28), crossed its ford (Genesis 32:22). But the LORD doesn't send Joshua there. He says, “…cross over the Jordan into the land that I am giving to the children of Israel.”

I see why that sounds right, but the LORD says otherwise. He tells Joshua, “I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread, just as I promised to Moses.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. So this promise was already made before Joshua ever heard it.

Right, friend, it isn't brand new. The LORD says, “I have given you every place where the sole of your foot will tread, just as I promised to Moses.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. Joshua is hearing a promise that was made before him.

That's not what the LORD says, friend. He tells Joshua, “No one shall stand against you all the days of your life.” Not a few, not some. No one. So there is no warning about enemies who can still stand.

That's it. The LORD says, “No one shall stand against you all the days of your life.” There is no list of exceptions, and no warning about a few who might still stand. When the LORD says no one, I'd take Him at His word.

Moses, Israel's leader, is the name the LORD gives. He says, “As I was with Moses, so will I be with you…” Joshua served as Moses' assistant, so he has seen up close what that looks like. Now it's his turn to have the LORD beside him.

Abraham, Israel's forefather, is a big name in the land promise, since God promised the land to his offspring (Genesis 12:7). But that's not the name in this verse. The LORD says, “As I was with Moses, so will I be with you…” Moses is the one Joshua just served beside.

Jacob, who was later called Israel (Genesis 32:28), is a fair guess for someone in the Bible neighborhood. But the LORD names someone else here. He says, “As I was with Moses, so will I be with you…” It's Moses, the leader Joshua just served beside.

Yes, friend! The LORD says, “Be strong and courageous…” He has just promised to be with Joshua, and now He gives him the command for the job. Joshua is about to lead a whole people into a new land, so I'd say that's the right thing to hear.
Those are good things to be, friend. But they're not the words the LORD speaks to Joshua here. He says, “Be strong and courageous…” That's the command for the job ahead.
Calm and gentle sound nice, and I could use more of both near a hot oven. But the LORD's command to Joshua is different. He says, “Be strong and courageous…”

explanations.answer: He will give the people the land
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the LORD gives. He says, “Be strong and courageous, for you shall give these people the inheritance of the land that I swore to their fathers I would give them.” The land is the LORD's promise, and Joshua is the one who will hand it over. That's a big delivery job.

explanations.answer: He will build the LORD a temple
explanations.explanation: No temple shows up in this passage, friend. The LORD says why Joshua needs courage: “…you shall give these people the inheritance of the land that I swore to their fathers I would give them.” The job is about the land.

explanations.answer: He will judge the people's disputes
explanations.explanation: Judging disputes isn't mentioned here. The LORD tells Joshua, “…you shall give these people the inheritance of the land that I swore to their fathers I would give them.” That's the reason for the strength and courage. It's about giving them the land.

You've got it, friend. The LORD says, “Be careful to observe all the law that My servant Moses commanded you.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua, and the law he gave is what Joshua is told to keep close. Courage and care go together here.

explanations.answer: All the customs of the land
explanations.explanation: The LORD doesn't point Joshua to the customs of the land. He says, “Be careful to observe all the law that My servant Moses commanded you.” That's the law Joshua has been given, from Moses, Israel's leader.

explanations.answer: All the orders of the elders
explanations.explanation: The elders aren't mentioned in these verses. The LORD says, “Be careful to observe all the law that My servant Moses commanded you.” It's the law, not a pile of orders from somebody else.
True, friend. The LORD says, “Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may prosper wherever you go.” It's like walking a straight line down the middle of a road. Stay on it.

It's actually in the text, friend. The LORD says, “Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may prosper wherever you go.” So that statement is true. Straight down the middle, no swerving.

Day and night, friend. The LORD says, “This Book of the Law must not depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night…” That's morning, evening and every hour between. I can barely keep a batch from burning, so I'm impressed.
Once a week is a good habit, but it's not what the LORD says. He tells Joshua, “…meditate on it day and night…” That's a lot more often than every Sabbath.
Once a month would be easy on the schedule, but the LORD asks for much more. He says, “…meditate on it day and night…” No waiting for the moon to come around.

Do, friend! The LORD says to meditate on it “…so that you may be careful to do everything written in it.” It isn't just to have the words in his head. It's to do what the Book says. Reading a recipe never fed anybody, and I would know.
Memorizing is a good thing to do, but it's not the word the LORD uses. He says, “…so that you may be careful to do everything written in it.” The goal is doing.
Explaining is a fine skill, but that's not the word here. The LORD tells Joshua to meditate on the Book “…so that you may be careful to do everything written in it.” The goal is doing it.
Yes, friend. Joshua tells the officers to say, “Prepare your provisions…” That means food for the road. I like that plan, because nobody should cross a river hungry.
Offerings aren't mentioned in this message. Joshua tells the officers to say, “Prepare your provisions…” Provisions are what the people will need for the journey ahead.

Winter isn't in this message, friend. Joshua tells the officers to say, “Prepare your provisions, for within three days you will cross the Jordan…” The people are told to get provisions ready, and the crossing is three days away.

explanations.answer: To take possession of the land
explanations.explanation: That's it. Joshua's message says they will “…go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.” The crossing is about the land the LORD is giving. Three days is not much time to pack.

explanations.answer: To find water for the camp
explanations.explanation: Water for the camp isn't the reason given. Joshua's message says they will cross “…to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.” That's the whole point of the trip.

explanations.answer: To meet the army of Moab
explanations.explanation: Moab's army doesn't come up in this message. Joshua says they will cross “…to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.” The reason is the land.

True, friend. Joshua says, “Your wives, your young children, and your livestock may remain in the land that Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. Their families stay where they are, and the men get ready to go.

That statement is actually true. Joshua tells those tribes, “Your wives, your young children, and your livestock may remain in the land that Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. So the families stay put.

explanations.answer: Cross over armed ahead of their brothers
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Joshua says, “…all your mighty men of valor must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers and help them…” Their own land is already settled, but they cross first to help. That's showing up for family.

explanations.answer: Stay behind and guard their families
explanations.explanation: The families do stay, but that's not the job for the mighty men of valor. Joshua says they “…must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers and help them…” The men cross first.

explanations.answer: Go back and guard the land of Moab
explanations.explanation: Guarding Moab isn't mentioned, friend. Joshua says, “…all your mighty men of valor must be armed for battle to cross over ahead of your brothers and help them…” Their job is to cross over and help.

Not quite, friend. Joshua says they cross over to help “…until the LORD gives them rest as He has done for you, and your brothers also possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them.” Only then may they return home. Crossing alone doesn't end the job.

That's right. Joshua says they help “…until the LORD gives them rest as He has done for you, and your brothers also possess the land…” Then they may return to their own land. The job lasts until their brothers have their land too.
That's what they say, friend. “Everything you have commanded us we will do, and everywhere you send us we will go.” They don't ask for time or say maybe. It's a full yes.

explanations.answer: To think it over for a while
explanations.explanation: There's no thinking it over in their answer. They say, “Everything you have commanded us we will do, and everywhere you send us we will go.” It's an answer ready to go right away.

explanations.answer: To wait for a sign from heaven
explanations.explanation: They don't ask for a sign, friend. Their answer is, “Everything you have commanded us we will do, and everywhere you send us we will go.” No waiting involved.
True, friend. They say, “Just as we obeyed Moses in all things, so we will obey you.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. They are saying that what they gave Moses, Joshua will get too.
That statement is actually in the text. They tell Joshua, “Just as we obeyed Moses in all things, so we will obey you.” Moses was Israel's leader before Joshua. So the promise is true as stated.

explanations.answer: They will be put to death
explanations.explanation: That's what they say, friend, and it's a serious line. They tell Joshua, “Anyone who rebels against your order and does not obey your words, all that you command him, will be put to death.” I think this is one of the heavy parts of the passage. They aren't joking around.

explanations.answer: They will be sent out of camp
explanations.explanation: Being sent out of camp is not what they say. Their words are, “Anyone who rebels against your order and does not obey your words, all that you command him, will be put to death.” I think it's a heavy line. They aren't joking around.

explanations.answer: They will pay a heavy fine
explanations.explanation: A fine isn't in their answer. They say, “Anyone who rebels against your order and does not obey your words, all that you command him, will be put to death.” I think this is one of the heavy lines in the passage.
